sources.entry: grab/front-end-guide: a study guide and introduction to the modern front end stack.

summary.one_liner: A study guide from Grab's web team that walks newcomers through the modern JavaScript front end stack (SPAs, React, Redux, Jest, ESLint, Flow, webpack, Yarn, CI and deployment) and explains why each tool was chosen.
summary.what_it_does: The guide is organized as a sequence of sections, each covering one part of front end development: single-page apps, ES2015 and Babel, React, Flux/Redux state management, CSS Modules, testing with Jest and Enzyme, linting with ESLint and stylelint, Prettier formatting, Flow types, webpack, Yarn, Travis CI, static hosting on S3 with CloudFront, Ansible Tower deployment, and Sentry monitoring. Each section explains the reasoning behind the recommendation, names alternatives, gives an estimated learning duration, and lists study links. It is explicitly aimed at back end engineers and newcomers to front end work, and it describes how Grab uses these tools rather than offering a generic tutorial. The README is a long essay with links, not a runnable project, so the content is conceptual and opinionated.
use_cases: onboard new engineers to a modern JavaScript stack
learn React and Redux from a recommended order
understand single-page app versus server-side rendering tradeoffs
set up a CI pipeline that builds and uploads static bundles
pick linting, formatting and type-checking tools for a team
notable: Explains the reasoning behind each tool choice, not just setup steps
Each section gives an estimated learning duration and alternatives
Describes how Grab's real pipeline runs: Travis CI to S3 tar builds to Ansible Tower deployment
Covers the SPA routing flow for serving index.html from S3 or Nginx
caveats: Opinionated and tied to choices made by Grab's team as of 2017, so some recommendations (for example Flow over TypeScript, Travis CI, npm 5 comparison) may be dated
Not a runnable project or code library; it is a written study guide
README is truncated in the provided text, so the final reading list is not visible
